newsitem.title: USA: Lumber prices soar on tight supplies.
newsitem.headline: Lumber prices soar on tight supplies.

text.p: Lumber futures jumped again Wednesday to post limit-up gains on strong demand and rising prices in the cash market.
Gasoline prices fell on profit-taking after recent steep gains. Gold and silver edged higher.
Lumber analysts said quotas on Canadian lumber exports, strong demand from builders, and expected holiday shutdowns at lumber mills all fuelled recent price gains in the cash and futures markets.
Random Lengths, a lumber industry newsletter, quoted cash spruce at $394 for 1,000 board feet Wednesday, up $16 from a week ago. But industry sources said by late Wednesday there were $400 trades.
Spruce is widely used for wall studs in home contruction and Canada is the leading supplier to the U.S. market.
"Cash (trade) got quiet busy late in the afternoon on Tuesday, after the futures had closed, and continued busy this morning," said Curt Cunningham, president of Pacific Futures Trading.
Cash business increased after the Thanksgiving Day holiday and there was buying dealers, partly on concerns that sawmills will be shutting down for the holidays.

"The (Canadian) quota is still in force and mills are extremely short (of logs)," said Tim Elrod, a lumber trader at pacific Futures, adding large amounts of lumber were being shipped to Japan and Europe.
"There just isn't much wood out there," said Elrod, who said futures prices could top $500 by early next year.
Lumber for January delivery rose the $10 daily limit to $409.30 for 1,000 board feet and March rose $10 to $395.30 at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.
A week-old refinery workers strike at the French oil giant Elf Aquitaine had spurred buying on Monday and Tuesday. On Wednesday, gasoline reached strong technical resistance near 70 cents a gallon.
"The market needed to decide whether it was going to push gasoline through 70 cents or not, and at the end it gave up on the attempt," said Tim Evans, analyst with Pegasus Econometric Group.

January gasoline fell 0.89 cent to 68.24 cents a gallon at the New York Mercantile Exchange. January heating oil, pressured by bearish inventory data, lost 0.65 cent to 73.57 cents a gallon and January crude oil fell 13 cents to $24.80 a barrel, pressured by losses in refined products.

The American Petroleum Institute said after trading closed on Tuesday that stocks of heating oil and diesel fuel grew 1.8 million barrels last week. The Energy Information Administration said Wednesday morning that its own inventory report showed distillate stocks swelled 3.9 million barrels.
Gold and silver edged higher as prices rebounded from contract lows on Tuesday.

A sharp drop in stock markets Tuesday and Wednesday may have steered some investors to precious metals, but metals traders said a much bigger stock market decline would be needed to prompt an exodus to precious metals.
February gold rose $2.10 to $372.50 an ounce and March silver gained 1.7 cents to $4.862 an ounce at New York's Commodity Exchange.
